<document>
From: Dana Whitfield, Maple Court Apartments
Subject: Late fee - Unit 3B

Hi,

Our records show this month's rent was received on the 3rd. As you know, rent is due
on the 1st, so a late fee of $75 has been added to your account. We were disappointed
to see this, since on-time payments help us keep the building running for everyone.
We'd appreciate it if you could be more careful going forward. Please pay the fee
along with next month's rent.

Thanks for understanding,
Dana

---
Lease excerpt (Maple Court residential lease):
Section 4.1: Rent is $1,450 per month, payable by check, money order, or the resident
portal.
Section 4.2: Rent is due on the 1st. A grace period applies through the 5th; no late
fees may be charged during the grace period.
Section 4.3: Returned payments incur a $35 fee.
Section 9.4: Notices to the landlord must be in writing and may be sent by email.
</document>

Here's a draft you can send by email, which Section 9.4 permits:

**Subject: Dispute of Late Fee - Unit 3B**

Hi Dana,

Thank you for your message regarding the $75 late fee on Unit 3B. I've reviewed my lease, and I believe the fee was applied in error.

Section 4.2 of the lease states that rent is due on the 1st, with a grace period through the 5th, and that no late fees may be charged during the grace period. My rent for this month was received on the 3rd, which falls within that grace period. Because of this, the $75 charge does not appear to be consistent with the terms of my lease.

I'd appreciate it if you could review the payment record and remove the $75 fee from my account. Please confirm once this has been corrected. If you believe I'm reading the lease differently, I'm happy to discuss it and look at the relevant language together.

I value my tenancy at Maple Court and want to keep my account in good standing, so I appreciate your attention to this.

Thank you,
[Your name]
Unit 3B
[Date]

---

Before sending, you may want to keep a copy of your payment confirmation showing the date it was received, and save this email thread in case you need to escalate. If the fee isn't removed, you could also check whether your state or city has rules on late fees that would apply.
